conclusion: A single current-main HIP 7.15 one-queue process with same-stream retirement markers after every prefill layer completes the full 128K warmup+3 protocol exactly, whereas each of the three preceding chunk-marker processes entered persistent no-progress within zero or one measured pass. All four layer-marked prefills retire through the final sample marker with no cursor lag; the three measured passes are tightly grouped at 503.732 median prefill and 28.246 median decode tok/s, and every pass returns token 9707. This is evidence that the layer-marker perturbation may suppress the failure by altering queue packetization/progress, but it does not establish stability or a production workaround: only one process was run, the defect is intermittent, and each marker is a tiny system-fence kernel writing host-mapped memory. A repeated-process gate and a decoupled heartbeat A/B require separate approval/evidence.

instrumentation.interpretation_boundary: One completed instrumented process is not a reliability result and cannot prove that markers fixed the lifecycle defect.
